events.title: Battle of Kosovo
events.description: Ottoman forces under Sultan Murad I faced a Serbian-led coalition on the field of Kosovo. The battle was hard-fought, and it opened the way for Ottoman expansion across Southeastern Europe.
events.significance: The battle became a lasting symbol in Serbian memory and is still commemorated each year on Vidovdan.

events.title: Queen Victoria Is Crowned
events.description: At Westminster Abbey, the 19-year-old Victoria was crowned Queen of the United Kingdom. Her reign was to last more than 63 years.
events.significance: Her reign gave its name to the Victorian era, a period of industrial growth, imperial expansion and social change in Britain.

events.title: Adolphe Sax Patents the Saxophone
events.description: Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax received a patent for his new brass-and-reed invention, the saxophone.
events.significance: The saxophone became central to jazz, popular music and the modern orchestra.

events.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
events.description: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria and his wife Sophie were shot dead in Sarajevo by the Serb nationalist Gavrilo Princip.
events.significance: The killings set off a chain of diplomatic crises that led to the outbreak of World War I.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles Signed
events.description: Germany and the Allied powers signed the Treaty of Versailles in France, five years to the day after the Sarajevo assassination.
events.significance: The treaty formally ended World War I and reshaped the map of Europe. Its terms remained a source of bitter dispute in the years that followed.
